steps.text: Place grated zucchini in a clean kitchen towel or on paper towels and squeeze tightly to remove excess water.
Place drained zucchini in a medium bowl. Add beaten eggs, flour, Parmesan cheese, mozzarella cheese, onion, and salt; stir until well combined.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Working in batches, scoop tablespoonfuls of zucchini mixture into hot oil. Fry until crisp and golden brown, about 2 minutes per side.

raw_recipe.headline: Zucchini Patties
raw_recipe.description: Crispy cheesy zucchini patties make a lovely change from potato pancakes during summer squash season. Serve with tomato sauce or sour cream on top.

video.description: Watch how to make a different type of pancake. These savory pancakes or patties are made with grated zucchini. Serve them up with tomato sauce or sour cream for a quick and easy appetizer. They are also fantastic at breakfast with a soft boiled egg.

review.reviewBody: This is a very good recipe which I will definitely use again. After reading other reviews, I made a couple adjustments. I salted the grated zucchini first and let it sit in a colander to draw out the excess moisture. Then I patted it dry with paper towels. I also added some fresh chopped garlic and Italian-style bread crumbs to the mixture. Then, after forming the patties, I patted on more bread crumbs. They fried up nice and crispy. I served them with marinara sauce, which my husband and I both thought was the perfect accompaniment.
These are delicious! I substituted instant mashed potato flakes for the flour, which I think makes for better taste and consistency!

WOW! These are soooo good! Very easy to make. I tweaked the recipe a bit though since it seemed a little bland as is. I added some black pepper, parsley and garlic. I also threw in some chopped mushrooms since they go so well with zucchini. I think next time I'll try different cheeses and other complementary veggies like red bell pepper. These would probably go really well with some marinara sauce too.

I make these patties all the time. For a more healthy way I bake them in a jelly roll pan at 375 for 20 min then turn them and bake for an additional 15. Time depends on your oven, the size of the patties and thickness. I spray the bottom of the pan with PAM. I squeeze as much water out of the zucchini as possible and I don't use salt. The salt makes the zucchini more runny. There is enough salt in the cheeses and you can always salt them after they are baked. I also use 1/2 cup of pepper jack cheese and 1/2 cup of feta instead of the mozzarella cheese. These cheeses give the patties a better taste. I don't use any oil or flour in my patties. I use Italian bread crumbs I also double the recipe but don't double the eggs.

I tweaked the recipe a bit to suit my family's taste (as most people do) and we LOVE it! I salted the zucchini and let it drain for about 15 minutes, substituted 1/2 the flour with seasoned bread crumbs (used gluten free flour and crumbs), added garlic powder and smoked paprika. Finally, I pre-cooked the onion with green pepper and shredded carrots, and then mixed it all together and cooked as the recipe states, topping with salt while they drain on paper towel. Dangerously good, I could eat the entire batch myself. This will definitely remain in our rotation forever!

Lessons learned: 1) Didn't have a clue how many zuccs to buy. Told the wife 3 or 4 to be on the safe side. She got 6 (bogo). Turns out ONE good sized zucc will make you a cup of shredded, so I made a double batch. 2) I use decent quality stainless fry pans (Misen) and the recommended heat was way too high for me. I had to go below halfway (hair under medium) to keep them from burning. 3) I tended to try to make the patties too large. Better off with smaller/flatter so they cook through in the time that they brown. 4) I felt like they needed more seasoning so I will experiment next time with some Sunny Paris blend (Penzys) in the mix, probably some pepper, who knows what else. Definitely will make again. Piece of cake if you have a food processor.

This recipe is amazing! I did use a previous poster s advice and used half potato flakes with the flour. I added a pinch of dano’s seasoning. The game changer was I used the waffle maker, no oil or butter needed!!

I used instant potato flakes, as several comments have recommended I'm not gonna lie, I was panicking when I was mixing these up, and my mixture seemed very dry (I had squeezed the shredded zucchini in some cheesecloth before combining the ingredients). But I continued with the process, and these turned out wonderfully. While they weren't the prettiest thing I'd ever made, they have a very good flavor and all considered, I think they were easier than zucchini parmesan. I made them on Sunday, and I plan to reheat them through the week, to serve with a side of spaghetti and sauce.

Salted the grated zucchini and squeezed dry in towel to remove excess water, the proceeded as directed except followed the suggestion to use potato flakes instead of flour. Mixed some store-bought pesto with Greek yogurt as garnish- delicious! And not that much effort!

These are so delicious hot or cold. We keep them in the fridge for snacking, they are SO satisfying and healthy. I make up several batches, place them on cookie sheets in the freezer until partly frozen, then bag them up in portions of 12. Take them out and cook them fresh every few days, they are so simple and lived by everyone!

So good! Added garlic powder, onion powder and white pepper and cooked in the waffle iron. Whipped up a sauce using 1/2 cup plain Greek yogurt, 1/2 cup sour cream, garlic powder, salt, 1 tsp dried dill, 1 tablespoon lemon juice, 1 tablespoon olive oil.

Loved this recipe combined with another. I added a grain rice/veggie mix that I had prepared. Also grated Gouda cheese and half cheddar. Served it with a cream cheese/bacon mayo mix for a spread or side dip! Excellent. Also grated a small squash to add to the zucchini!!

Used potato flakes instead of flour. Squeezed the zucchini after threading and added the cheese and potato and eggs. Was not watery at all. Fried till golden. Hubby said they tasted like potato pancakes and fritters. We ate them all. No leftovers
These are a big hit in my house, even for the "meat eaters". I didn't change anything other than salt the shredded zucchini for 30 min before squeezing out liquid.
Very good when you have a lot of zucchini.
Delicious! Use 1/2 flour and 1/2 cornstarch to achieve crispness.
My Momma Maria zucchini pancakes. For the Greek in us!
A lot of steps but good use of your zucchini - shredded with my new geedel rotary grater got from Amazon and made it easier. Also added onion flakes since I had none and diced a bit of red peppers.

These remind my family of a favorite Japanese dish - okonmiaki. Those pancakes, just like these can be altered to include almost any left over veggie in your fridge - cabbage, crook neck squash, bell peppers, etc etc. I added flax meal and used cashew mozzarella and gluten free flour to up the healthy factor. Also added seasoning on the savory side - aglio olio and paprika. Super tasty, going into our regular rotation!
Terrific recipe! I should have doubled it
